title: Tenant-aware burst policy and economics lab
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Build an experiment-driven lab to evaluate tenant-aware burst policies and produce concrete right-sizing recommendations and utilization reports for Dedicated fleets.

Background: Customers with Dedicated pools request throughput guarantees for bursty traffic (seasonal launches, promotions, or unpredictable spikes). Our current autoscale presets are conservative and either overcommit capacity (higher cost) or under-serve transient demand (missed SLOs). There is limited tooling to (a) quantify tenant-level burst economics, (b) compare autoscale policy variants under realistic mixes, and (c) produce prescriptive commit/slot recommendations.

Scope:
- Instrument a replay-based simulation harness to run candidate autoscale policies against historical tenant traffic (prefix replay + synthetic spike injections).
- Define a set of policy families: rapid-reactive, lookahead-predictive (short-window forecasting), and conservative-margin. Include hybrid burst credit bucket variant to allow short bursts without immediate scale.
- Collect economics signals: token-based cost delta, slot-hours consumed, p50/p95/p99 generation latency, SLO violations, and estimated missed revenue impact.
- Produce per-tenant recommendations: suggested commit change (up/down), suggested burst buffer (slot credit minutes), and expected cost delta with confidence bands.
- Add a one-page utilization report prototype and an insights feed for Account owners (Console + CSV export).

Success criteria (MVP):
- Simulation harness can replay 30 days of tenant traffic in <6 hours for a 100-tenant sample.
- Produce actionable recommendations for at least 80% of high-usage tenants in the sample (recommendations include delta and rationale).
- Observability: dashboards with 1) policy A vs B cost and SLO curves, 2) tenant-level burst exposure heatmap.

Deliverables:
1) Simulation harness (repo: infra/dedicated/burst-lab) and a runnable notebook to reproduce experiments.
2) Console mock for "Burst Economics" one-pager and CSV export.
3) PR to runtime to expose slot-credit telemetry and a light-weight sampling hook.
4) Findings doc with top 20 tenant recommendations and rollout playbook.

Acceptance criteria:
- Design review approved by Runtime and Product (notes linked).
- Lab runs for two real customers (anonymized) and yields recommendations with measured cost vs SLO impact.
- Follow-up ticket(s) created for policy rollout automation and billing adjustments.
comments: 2025-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, Product, and Customer Success. Agreed goals and measurement thresholds. Assigned Liam as owner for harness and R&D. Action: capture historical traffic slices and SLO definitions.

2025-02-18 - Liam O'Connor: First prototype of replay harness committed to infra/dedicated/burst-lab. Able to replay a single-tenant day in ~14 minutes with synthetic spikes. Need to optimize batching of requests in harness to approach target throughput.

2025-02-23 - Runtime review: Discussed telemetry gaps. Runtime team to add slot-credit and open-slot metrics; tentative patch submitted (PR #842). Observability: add per-tenant slot-usage tag to Prometheus export.

2025-02-28 - Product feedback: Requested clear recommendation format (delta slots, recommended commit, expected monthly cost delta, 90% CI) and short plain-language rationale for each tenant. Also asked for CSV template for account teams.

2025-03-03 - Simulation run: 30-day replay across 50 high-usage tenants completed. Early findings: predictive policy reduced SLO violations by 68% vs conservative baseline while increasing slot-hours by 12% (median). Reactive policy reduced cost but had a higher p99 latency spike during large bursts. Added a new hybrid credit-bucket policy to test.

2025-03-06 - Blocker noted by Liam: Need tenant mapping from billing to runtime tenant IDs for accurate cost attribution. CS team flagged data access constraint for one customer; working with Privacy to get anonymized export.
